payload: A 3D-printing news roundup from 'Mike': Prusa Core 1L and Core 1 tool-changer pre-order pricing, a first look at Creality's K3 Cleatech tool changer, and three patent/product items (HeyGears automated resin removal, Adam Form/Mova nozzle changer, Sunlu dry cabinet).

points.label: Prusa Core 1L & Core 1 pre-orders (with 'index' tool-changer system)
points.detail: Core 1L (not shown yet): $2,989 for 8-tool, $2,739 for 4-tool, ships Nov 5. Core 1 fully outfitted with the index: just under $2,000 base and $2,249 for the 8-tool version, ships Oct 15. Mike suggests splurging for the 8-tool.

points.label: Creality K3 Cleatech (first look) + K3 Pro
points.detail: Tool changer shown only via Reddit images; Mike thinks it resembles Creality's budget Spark series and 'looks cheap.' A gray 'Pro' variant also appeared. ~$595 list in China; with a ~40.6% US tariff he guesses ~$600-700 retail, and thinks $800 would push buyers to the proven Anycubic U1.

points.label: HeyGears automated resin-removal patent
points.detail: Per a Fabaloo article, HeyGears patented a device that circulates air to pull leftover resin off finished prints (falling back into the vat), a step toward automated at-scale resin printing. A concept/patent, not a shipping product.

points.label: Adam Form / Mova nozzle-changer patent
points.detail: An additional patent covering their nozzle changer; Mike doubts a nozzle changer is viable at their planned price and asks whether they should pivot to a tool-changer index style. Some backers had deposits refunded, others still pending.

points.label: Sunlu dry cabinet (unreleased product)
points.detail: Keeps already-dry filament dry (it does not dry wet filament); holds up to 10 spools; Mike plans to use it for PETG/ASA/ABS. Available for pre-order with a $1 deposit to lock the price. Disclosed as sent to him at no cost.

notes: Intro promises delivered: two tool changers (Prusa Core, Creality K3), an 'unreleased product' (Sunlu cabinet), and a couple of patents (HeyGears, Mova).
Ends with a plug for a Friday-night livestream ~7pm Arizona time.
gaps: Mike says the Creality K3 price converts 'from yen,' but Creality is a Chinese company, so the ~$595 figure is almost certainly yuan/RMB — likely a misstatement.
The tariff analysis (~40.6% rate, a $350 customs value, $142 duty) is self-admittedly generated by ChatGPT ('my research is ChatGPT'), i.e., an unverified estimate rather than sourced data.
